columns_never_fillable.reason: This is a healthcare REIT — all properties are hospitals or nursing homes. Neither the Portfolio Statement nor the property cards disclose NLA. Size metric across all properties is GFA (gross floor area) in m², plus beds/rooms where applicable. Confirmed by reading all property overview pages (pp. 28-43) and Portfolio Statement (pp. 135-145).

Per-property NPI is not disclosed anywhere in the report. The audited Statement of Total Return only shows Group-level NPI of S$97,340,000. No segment-level or per-property NPI table is present. The report provides only per-property 'Rental Income' (marketing figures in S$ millions on the property cards) which is NOT the same as NPI. Confirmed by searching all financial notes.

Per-property trade mix is not disclosed. This is a master-lease REIT with one master lessee per property (or co-lessee structure), so sub-tenant breakdown is not disclosed. Confirmed by reading all property overview pages.

data_with_no_home.description: Maximum beds/rooms per property (healthcare capacity metric)
data_with_no_home.note: Disclosed on property overview pages (pp. 28-43). Portfolio total: 6,305 beds/rooms as at 31 Dec 2025. Per property: Indonesia total 3,946, Japan total 1,655 rooms, Singapore total 704 beds. GFA/NLA are not healthcare operating metrics; beds/keys are. These should be captured in a healthcare-specific extension field.

Japan: average rate SGD 1 = JPY 112 (for income/revenue); closing rate SGD 1 = JPY 120 (for valuation as at 31 Dec 2025). Indonesia: average rate SGD 1 = IDR 12,346 (for income); closing rate SGD 1 = IDR 12,987 (for valuation as at 31 Dec 2025).

data_with_no_home.description: Distribution income by contract type and geography (not trade mix)
data_with_no_home.note: Revenue breakdown by geography: Indonesia 82.5% (S$82.9M), Japan 13.3% (S$13.4M), Singapore 4.2% (S$4.2M). Also: income model breakdown — Indonesia: hospital/mall MLAs restructured in 2021 with Siloam and LPKR as co-lessees; Japan: master leases with independent nursing home operators; Singapore: master leases with nursing home operators.

data_with_no_home.description: Strategic Review ongoing — potential sale of Indonesian hospital assets
data_with_no_home.note: As at 31 December 2025, a Strategic Review is ongoing following Siloam's LOI to acquire First REIT's Indonesia hospital portfolio. This is a material disclosure but does not affect the financial data for FY2025.

PT Metropolis Propertindo Utama (MPU) has rental outstanding of approximately IDR 89,253,766,000 (~S$6,873,000) as at 31 December 2025. IDR 43,365,038,000 (~S$3,339,000) relates to mall properties and IDR 45,888,728,000 (~S$3,534,000) to hospital properties. Security deposit of IDR 50,532,034,000 (~S$3,891,000) available to cover the hospital outstanding.
S$33,282,000 perpetual securities outstanding. Total return attributable to perpetual securities holders in FY2025: S$1,656,000. These are deducted from total return attributable to unitholders.

parsing_traps: Portfolio Statement uses one table per property across multiple pages (pp. 136-145) with stacked cells: property name, address, acquisition date, property type, land title type, lease term, and remaining lease term all in one cell — this is the 'Stacked-cell, one-table-per-property' shape flagged in REFERENCE.md §2 as not deterministically parseable. LLM extraction was used.

Property cards (pp. 28-43) disclose 'FY2025 Rental Income' in S$ millions rounded to 1 decimal place — this is a marketing figure, NOT the audited rental income. Do not confuse with the audited figure in Note 16 (S$100,526,000 Group total). Used for per-property gross_revenue as the only per-property figure available.

The Singapore properties disclose 'FRS 116 adjustment on rental straight-lining' separately. The FY2025 Rental Income on property cards is 'Without FRS 116 Adjustment on rental straight-lining'. The Group Note 16 includes straight-lining adjustment of S$7,446,000. Group-level reconciliation of Note 16 total (S$100,531,000) includes straight-lining; per-property cards exclude it.

Japan property appraised values on cards are disclosed in both JPY and SGD (converted at end-period rate SGD 1 = JPY 120). The audited Portfolio Statement values are the authoritative carrying values and differ slightly from the converted card values due to rounding.

Imperial Aryaduta Hotel & Country Club: divested December 2025. Market valuation = nil (S$0) in Portfolio Statement as at 31/12/2025. Prior year value was S$27,723,000. Loss on disposal recognised S$7,535,000.

Trade mix table on p.5 is labelled 'Rental Income by Trade Sector Mix' before FRS 116 straight-lining adjustments, denominator = rental income (not GRI excl. GTO). Three trade sectors disclosed: Healthcare 89.4%, Hospitality 5.6%, Retail 5.0%.
Top tenants table on p.5 shows ALL 11 tenants (100% of rental income). This is every tenant, not just the top 10 — First REIT has only 11 tenants total as at 31 December 2025.

reconciliation.gross_revenue_gap_explanation: Property card rental income figures are in S$ millions rounded to 1 decimal place. Sum of per-property card values = ~S$100.4M. Audited Note 16 total = S$100,531,000. Gap of ~S$131,000 is rounding noise in per-property cards. reconciliation.npi_note: Per-property NPI not disclosed. Only Group-level NPI (S$97,340,000) is audited. Note: Group-level NPI = Rental income S$100,531 - Property operating expenses S$3,191 = S$97,340,000.
